## The Anchoring Study

:::::: panel-tabset
#### Check-In

```{r}
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| include: false
library(googlesheets4)
library(gt)
library(tidyverse)
library(jtools)
options(knitr.kable.NA = "")
gs4_deauth()
anchor <- read_sheet("https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1hPzlbSV6fex0aJbEd4zPPmrNcdEGrp-5u4reqpVdQhI/edit?usp=sharing", sheet = "Form Responses 1")

# anchor <- read.csv("~/Downloads/9A_Eichstaedt_SP24.csv", stringsAsFactors = T)
names(anchor)
anchor <- anchor[,c(7, 9, 11:13, 15, 17:19)]
names(anchor) <- c("condition", "catH", "treeH", "have.catH", "hikeH",
                   "catL", "treeL", "have.catL", "hikeL")
head(anchor)

anchor$condition <- as.factor(anchor$condition)
levels(anchor$condition) <- c("LOW", "HIGH")

anchorH <- anchor[anchor$condition == "HIGH",]
anchorL <- anchor[anchor$condition == "LOW",]

names(anchorH)[1:5] <- c("condition", "cat", "tree", "have.cat", "do.hike")
names(anchorL)[c(1, 6:9)] <- c("condition", "cat", "tree", "have.cat", "do.hike")

anchor <- rbind(anchorH[,c(1:5)],
                anchorL[,c(1,6:9)])

## Data Cleaning

library(gplots)
hist(anchor$cat)
hist(anchor$tree)
anchor$tree[anchor$tree > 1500] <- NA
anchor$have.cat <- as.factor(anchor$have.cat)
anchor$do.hike <- as.factor(anchor$do.hike)
plot(anchor$condition)
plot(anchor$have.cat)
plot(anchor$do.hike)
```

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```         
dependent variable. what the researchers want to predict or explain

experimental manipulation. change only one thing about the variable

extraneous variables as “noise”. other factors that might influence the outcome variable

random assignment. the group people are put in is random; this ensures that all other variables that might affect the result are evenly split across the two groups 

placebo effects. when individuals in the study change their behavior if they expect something to have an effect

external validity. how much does the experimental manipulation represent what someone might experience in real life?

construct validity. how much does the manipulation actually change the variable of interest?

experimenter expectancy effects. if experimenters know what will happen to participants, they may change their behavior in ways that affect the results 
```
:::

#### Random Assignment

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plot(condition ~ have.cat, data = anchor)
plot(condition ~ do.hike, data = anchor)
```

#### Causing Differences

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false


mod1 <- lm(cat ~ condition, data = anchor)
mod2 <- lm(tree ~ condition, data = anchor)
par(mfrow = c(1,2))
plotmeans(cat ~ condition, data = anchor, connect = F,
          xlab = "Experimental Condition",
          ylab = "Guesses About Cat Speeds (MPH)")
plotmeans(tree ~ condition, data = anchor, connect = F,
          xlab = "Experimental Condition",
          ylab = "Guesses About Tree Heights (ft)")

export_summs(mod1, mod2,
             model.names = c("Cat Speeds", "Tree Heights"),
             coefs = c("Low Group" = "(Intercept)",
                       "Difference in High Group" = "conditionHIGH"),
             error_format = "",
             star = NULL)
```

# Part 2 : Experiments {.smaller}

### KEY IDEA : Watch out for Misleading Control Variables {.smaller}

**RECAP : the manipulation (A/B Testing) :** researchers create multiple groups (conditions) and change ONE THING (the IV) about a person’s experience in each group & observe the result (the DV).

**KEY IDEA : the comparison group matters!**

- a 1.5 hour research methods class DECREASES boredom compared to…

- a 1.5 hour research methods class INCREASES boredom compared to…

### Science is Hard : Power Posing

- What is the experimental / control condition?

- Is this a fair comparison / manipulation?

::::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
[![Carney et al (2010). Power Posing.](images/clipboard-3273747639.png)](https://faculty.haas.berkeley.edu/dana_carney/power.poses.PS.2010.pdf)

### Other Questions to Consider : Does the experiment have....

::: panel-tabset
#### placebo effects

Will individuals in the study change their behavior if they expect something to have an effect?

![](images/clipboard-3273758330.png)

#### external validity

How much does the experimental manipulation represent what someone might experience in real life?

![](images/clipboard-1011573524.png)

#### construct validity

How much does the manipulation actually change the variable of interest?

![](images/cyberball.gif){fig-align="center"}

#### expectancy effects

If experimenters know what will happen to participants, will they change their behavior in ways that affect the results?

![](images/clipboard-1046030223.png)
:::
